title: SYSK Selects: How do dogs perceive time?
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the 2009 episode "How Do Dogs Perceive Time?" Josh and Chuck open with a story about a Paris murder case where a dog named Scooby was used as a witness, then discuss what time is, circadian oscillators, and whether dogs use episodic or semantic memory to anticipate feeding. They examine researcher William Roberts' claim that animals are "stuck in time" and why they disagree, citing hoarding squirrels and banana-choice primate studies, and argue that the "animals can't be happy or self-aware" view is speciesist. The episode closes with listener mail ("Muppet mail") about the Muppets, including Jim Henson's University of Maryland connection, a Muppet Whatnot Workshop, a Sesame Street adult-disability reinterpretation, and a wedding at the Henson sound stage.
topics: dog as witness Paris court case

segments.title: Rerun intro and Paris dog witness story
segments.summary: Chuck introduces this Selects rerun of the dog time episode. Josh recounts a story about a Paris court case in which a dog named Scooby barked at an alleged perpetrator, raising questions about whether dogs have memory.
topics: dog as witness Paris court case

segments.title: What is time and circadian rhythms
segments.summary: The hosts discuss time as a human construct versus time as past, present and future. They explain circadian oscillators and the roughly 24-hour circadian rhythm that governs sleep, hunger and hormones.

segments.title: Dogs anticipating feeding time
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck compare how their dogs and cats anticipate mealtimes. They ask whether dogs predict feeding from past experience or from an internal clock.

segments.title: Episodic vs semantic memory
segments.summary: The hosts explain the difference between episodic memory, which recalls personal experiences, and semantic memory, which holds facts and learned skills. They use examples like learning chess and recalling breakfast.

segments.title: William Roberts and the stuck in time theory
segments.summary: The hosts describe researcher William Roberts' work on pigeons and primates and his conclusion that animals are stuck in time, living in the present without long-term episodic memory. They discuss squirrel food hoarding and banana-choice experiments and offer alternative explanations.

segments.title: Goldfish memory and speciesism
segments.summary: Josh mentions the goldfish memory myth and questions how it would be tested. The hosts argue that claims animals lack happiness or self-awareness can reflect speciesism, and that scientists may lack tests clever enough to know what animals experience.

segments.title: Wrap-up of main topic
segments.summary: Josh summarizes Roberts' view that dogs do not perceive time and live in the present, and says the hosts disagree. He suggests searching the website for more.

segments.title: Muppet mail
segments.summary: Listener mail about the Muppets: a University of Maryland Jim Henson studies program and bench statue, a Muppet Whatnot Workshop in New York, a costume designer aunt of Miss Piggy's designer, a reinterpretation of Sesame Street characters, a wedding at the Henson sound stage, and Ralph the Dog not being used since Henson's death.
